title: Prompt Gardener: token economy & exemplar pruning
content:
Personal scratchpad — Aisha Kapoor

Goal: lightweight heuristics for keeping high-signal exemplars while minimizing token cost and drift. Think of the prompt set as a small garden: prune redundant plants, compost negative exemplars, plant stratified seedlings for edge cases.

Motivation / constraints:
- Hosted usage: token budget matters; customers with bursty workflows need stable quality under small shot budgets.
- We want 3–5 exemplar sets that are compact (~120–250 tokens total) for low-latency routes.
- Keep human- understandable rules for curator workflow (so solutions can be semi-automated in Optimize).

High-level hypotheses:
1) Stratified exemplars (by length, style, and failure-type) give better worst-case performance than naive top-N similarity picks.
2) Removing exemplars that cause hallucination anchors reduces precision more than recall — useful tradeoff for retrieval-like tasks.
3) A token-aware score (quality / token_cost^alpha) surfaces non-obvious small exemplars that punch above weight.

Experimental plan (mini-run locally with hosted-sim):
- Setup: gpt-like eval harness (dev env), temperature=0.0 for deterministic checks, eval set=200 items with labeled error types.
- Compare 4 exemplar selection policies: random-3, sim-top-3, stratified-3 (short/medium/long), token-aware-top-3 (quality/token^0.7).
- Metrics: exact-match, partial F1, hallucination-rate (binary), average tokens per prompt.

Candidate exemplar sets (toy):
- Stratified-3 (S):
  1) Q: "Summarize key compliance obligations for small SaaS selling B2B in EU." A: "Key obligations include DPA updates, data minimization, lawful basis, subprocessors list, breach notification timeframe."
  2) Q: "Draft an apt subject line for support follow-up: customer reporting missing billing line." A: "Follow-up: we dug into your invoice — quick clarification and next steps"
  3) Q: "How to explain rate limiting to a non-technical PM?" A: "Rate limiting controls request volume to keep systems responsive, like a queue at rush hour."

- Sim-top-3 (sim): short semantically-similar items pulled by embedding nearest neighbors (kept full length).
- Token-aware-top-3 (T): prefer compact exemplars with high human eval scores.

Failure cases observed (early manual tests):
- Anchor hallucination: an exemplar that mentions a vendor trademark caused the model to hallucinate vendor-specific policies in unrelated queries. Removing that exemplar reduced hallucination by ~20% on affected slice.
- Long exemplar bleed: a long, verbose exemplar improved recall but introduced spurious procedural steps in many outputs; short-form replacement recovered precision.
- Style collapse: mixing exemplars with very different tones caused mid-output style switching (businessy -> casual). Stratified tone constraints help.

Quick micro-results (dev run, 50 examples each):
- random-3: EM 48%, hallucination 14%, avg tokens/prompt 360
- sim-top-3: EM 57%, hallucination 18%, avg tokens/prompt 540
- stratified-3: EM 61%, hallucination 12%, avg tokens/prompt 310
- token-aware-3: EM 59%, hallucination 10%, avg tokens/prompt 245
Notes: stratified gives best EM with modest token savings; token-aware minimizes tokens & hallucination but slightly lower EM.

Concrete few-shot templates to try (short):
- Template A (instruction + examples + explicit refusal):
  "You are a concise support assistant. If request asks for unsupported legal advice say: 'I cannot provide legal advice; consult counsel.'
  EX1: <ex1>
  EX2: <ex2>
  Q: <user_query>
  A:"

- Template B (schema-first, then examples):
  "Return JSON with keys: intent, answer, citations[]. Use short sentences.
  EXS...
  Q:..."

Notes on pruning heuristics (rules of thumb):
- If two exemplars are >0.92 embedding-similarity and have same label, drop longer one unless it holds unique negative examples.
- Prioritize exemplars that correct common LLM errors (hallucination, wrong-bias) even if slightly longer.
- Score = human_score / (1 + tokens/100)^0.7 — tune alpha.
- Keep at least one exemplar that explicitly demonstrates refusal / boundary behavior.

Operational ideas for Optimize productization:
- Provide "gardener mode" that suggests exemplar removes ranked by expected quality-per-token impact. Visualize tradeoff (EM vs tokens).
- Allow curator to pin exemplars (prevent removal) and mark "compost" (archive negative exemplars for offline analysis).
- Auto-detect anchor terms (entities that later cause hallucination) and flag them.

Outstanding questions & next experiments:
- What's the right alpha for token penalty across different model sizes? (run grid: 0.4, 0.7, 1.0)
- Can we learn to synthesize compact exemplars that keep the key signal from longer ones? (small distillation prompts)
- How do these heuristics interact with retrieval-augmented prompts (when we add docs after examples)?

Todo (short):
- [ ] Run full 200-sample eval for stratified vs token-aware (owner: Aisha)
- [ ] Add automated hallucination anchor detector to local harness (owner: Jonah)
- [ ] Flesh out gardener UI mock (owner: Priya)
